guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Notice the Part That Came Here

Some people don’t merely say that love feels inaccessible. They say, “No. I hate myself.”

I don’t want to argue you out of that. If hatred is what you find inside, it deserves an honest hearing.

But I also don’t want to overlook something else.

If you chose to open this article, come to therapy, ask somebody for help, or try again after deciding you were hopeless, something in you wanted something to be different.

Maybe it is hope. Maybe desperation. Curiosity. Fear. Duty. A refusal to keep suffering this way. Maybe it is love. We don’t have to decide.

Ask that part: “What were you hoping might happen when you brought me here?”

Follow that thread.
note: Turn 65 (2026-10-17): the guide after Simple Practices, part 2 of 4 (Notice the Part That Came Here), drafted under the heading "## Notice the Part That Came Here".
before: Taking the hostility out makes room for the warmth to get in. What people say helps the most, though, is letting their defenses down. If you've never felt safe being loved, the ego can act like a stiff security guard who checks everyone's ID twice, and vulnerability is the opening the feeling needs. Sometimes the warmth isn't gone at all. A cold or cynical part is just standing in front of it.
brief:
- the main point: some people answer "No. I hate myself"; that deserves an honest hearing, not an argument; but if you opened this, came to therapy, asked for help or tried again after deciding you were hopeless, something in you wanted things to be different (hope, desperation, curiosity, fear, duty, a refusal to keep suffering, maybe love; no need to decide); ask that part what it hoped might happen when it brought you here, and follow that thread
- what the dedup leaves to add (experiments/t65-guide/LM-DEDUP-REPORT.md, group 2): self-hatred as the reply to love, heard rather than argued (G2.1–2.2); showing up as proof some part wants change (G2.3); its possible motives (G2.4); asking what it hoped for, and following that (G2.5–2.6).
